To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a2-M inhibits the anticoagulants effects of PS by forming complexes with APC.

the anticoagulatory protein C pathway in cord and adult plasmas is suppressed by alpha 2-macroglubulin (a2M) in a dose-dependent manner, and that this suppression is due to a2M-induced formation of an APC/a2M complex, which is not formed with PS.

alpha 2-macro-globulin (a 2-M) inhibits the anticoagulants protein C/protein C/protein S (PS) pathway by forming complexes with protein C (APPC), thereby reducing the formation of the APC/ PS complex, resulting in enhanced prothrombin conversion and thrombin generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the APC/ PS pathway by the plasma protein a2-M and its impact on thrombin generation in newborns.
a novel aspect in the regulation of the anticoa-gulant APC/PS system, namely the influence of a2-M on prothrom-bin activation and thrombin formation in plasma.
a previously unknown mechanism by which a2-M enhances prothrombosis and might thus contribute to the increased risk of thrombosis in the neonatal period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a2-M acts as a pro-coagulant in cord plasma and a coagulation inhibitor in adult plasma.
the procoagulant effect of alpha2-macroglo-bulin on thrombin generation is more pronounced in cord plasma compared to adult plasma.
a2-M acts as a pro- and anticoagulant depending on the plasma concentration of PS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a2-M is a procoagulatory factor in newborns.
the anticoagulation system in cord plasma is less efficient than in adult plasma.
the prothrombotic effects of alpha2-macrogobulin are not only due to its direct effects on the coagulation cascade but also due to inhibition of the antithrombolytic protein C pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anticoagulation of a2-M is a complex process and that it depends on the concentrations of its cofactors and the presence of other proteins.
a2-M can act pro- or anticoagulantly depending on the presence of other proteins in the plasma.
a2-M is not only an anticoagulant, but also a procoagulatant.
